hints: Consider what happens when a travelling wave reaches a fixed end of the string.
Name the two waves that overlap on the string after reflection.
walkthrough: A wave travelling along the string reflects at a fixed end.
The incident and reflected waves have the same frequency and travel in opposite directions.
Their superposition forms a stationary wave with fixed nodes.

ai_rubric.observable: States that waves reflect at a fixed end of the string.
Explains that incident and reflected waves travelling in opposite directions superpose or interfere.

hints: Nodes never move from their equilibrium positions.
A quarter cycle after the straight-string position, P has its greatest downward displacement.
walkthrough: Keep the string at zero displacement at every marked node.
Draw smooth sinusoidal loops between successive nodes.
At P, draw the loop at maximum downward displacement.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws an approximately sinusoidal stationary-wave shape with zero displacement at nodes and maximum downward displacement at P.

hints: Use the wave speed and period to find the wavelength first.
Use the node pattern in Fig. 5.1 to express AB as a multiple of the wavelength.
walkthrough: The wavelength is λ = vT = 35 × 0.040 = 1.4 m.
The node pattern shows that AB spans 2.5 wavelengths.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses v = λ/T, or v = fλ with f = 1/T.
Uses the node pattern to obtain AB = 3.5 m.
